# Josupeit.Practices.Services

> Abstract base classes implementing the lifecycle contracts of `Josupeit.Practices.Services.Abstractions`: `Service` and `AsyncService`, each also as a `Disposable*` variant (adds `IDisposable`) and an `AsyncDisposable*` variant (adds `IDisposable` and `IAsyncDisposable`; netstandard2.1 and net8.0 only). You override the `On*` hooks; the base class validates every transition, exposes the transitional states, treats repeated same-direction calls as no-ops, rolls back when a hook throws, and offers opt-in pausing through `CanPause`. Lifecycle calls are not synchronized, and disposing does not stop the service. Targets netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1, and net8.0; depends only on the Abstractions package; lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Services` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Services`; the Abstractions package comes along transitively. All types live in the `Josupeit.Practices.Services` namespace, the same one as the interfaces. Six abstract base classes, named lifecycle-last and disposal-first:

- `Service` - synchronous lifecycle, no disposal
- `DisposableService` - synchronous lifecycle, `IDisposable`
- `AsyncDisposableService` - synchronous lifecycle, `IDisposable` and `IAsyncDisposable` (netstandard2.1 and net8.0 only)
- `AsyncService` - asynchronous lifecycle, no disposal
- `DisposableAsyncService` - asynchronous lifecycle, `IDisposable`
- `AsyncDisposableAsyncService` - asynchronous lifecycle, `IDisposable` and `IAsyncDisposable` (netstandard2.1 and net8.0 only)

Implement the abstract `OnStart`/`OnStop` (or `OnStartAsync`/`OnStopAsync`) hooks as `protected override`; optionally override `CanPause => true` with `OnPause`/`OnResume`. The lifecycle methods themselves are not virtual. Same-direction calls such as `Start` while `Running` are no-ops; conflicting calls throw `InvalidOperationException`; `Pause`/`Resume` throw `NotSupportedException` when `CanPause` is false. A hook that throws rolls the state back. In the async classes a counter-operation during a transition cancels it through the hook's token rather than performing a transition of its own. Token-less async overloads are, by contract, equivalent to passing `CancellationToken.None`. Protected `ThrowIfNotRunning`/`ThrowIfRunning`/`ThrowIfPaused`/`ThrowIfStopped` guard your own members. Lifecycle calls are not synchronized; disposing does not stop the service.

## Documentation

- [Complete reference](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Services/llms-full.txt): every class with its members and override points, the full transition table, rollback and cancellation semantics, guards, disposal, usage, and common mistakes. Load this to write code against the package.
- [PublicAPI.Shipped.txt](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Services/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt): analyzer-enforced inventory of the members present on every target framework; [netstandard2.1](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Services/PublicAPI.Shipped.netstandard2.1.txt) and [net8.0](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Services/PublicAPI.Shipped.net8.0.txt) list the additions on those frameworks. `abstract` marks required hooks, `virtual` optional ones; accessibility is not shown.
- [README](https://codeberg.org/DerPeit/Josupeit.Practices/raw/branch/main/src/Josupeit.Practices.Services/README.md): human-oriented package overview as shown on NuGet.
